title: A New Generation Enters Real Estate: How Gen Z Is Making Its Mark
summary: Two Gen Z REMAX agents share what drew them to the profession, how they got started and what they've learned about building a business.
body_markdown:
As Gen Z navigates a challenging job market, more young people are pursuing careers that offer greater independence and flexibility. According to[LinkedIn’s 2026 Grad’s Guide](https://protect.checkpoint.com/v2/r01/___https:/www.linkedin.com/uzqxjdqnspjins-lwfix-lznij-757*~*-qnspjins-sjBx-xAuvjd___.YzJ1OnRoZXJlYWxicm9rZXJhZ2UyMTpjOmdvb2dsZV9tYWlsX2F0dGFjaG1lbnQ6NjM2OGJhYWQ0YzM5YWM0NjJlMDhmNzgxZGM3NDJiYzI6Nzo0NmZiOjg0ZWMwN2QxYzBiYTAzMjljYjQxNGVjNmZlYzFkZjlmOTU3ZDBmNWY2NDk1NWZkMWZmNDQyOWIxYzIzYmZlMDY6cDpUOlQ) , real estate is the second-fastest-growing industry for recent college graduates.


REMAX agents Elliott Quillo, 23, and Maddie Mittelsteadt, 29, are members of Gen Z who took different paths into real estate, but both were drawn to the opportunity to build something of their own.


**Two Agents, Two Different Paths**


Just three months into college, Elliott Quillo wanted something different.


He was studying nursing but knew the traditional nine-to-five wasn’t for him. At 19, he left school and earned his real estate license, eager to start a new career.


“When I first jumped into real estate at 19, I didn’t really know what I was getting into,” said Quillo, an agent with REMAX Plus in New Albany, Indiana. “I just knew it was an opportunity to have a business of my own.”


Four years later, Quillo continues to build his real estate business and sees more young people considering the same career path.


Maddie Mittelsteadt followed a more traditional route. After college, she began working for a homebuilder in Central Wisconsin, starting as a marketing coordinator and advancing to vice president of operations. Along the way, she discovered a passion for sales, operations and collaborating with others.


At 25, she decided to pursue a career in real estate, joining REMAX Excel in Schofield, Wisconsin.


“I decided that if I was going to pour my heart and energy into something, I wanted to build something of my own – my way,” she said.


##


Elliott Quillo, REMAX Plus, Albany, Indiana


##


Maddie Mittelsteadt, REMAX Excel, Schofield, Wisconsin


**Building Credibility at a Young Age**


Starting a career as a real estate agent at a young age requires building trust and credibility.


“How do you get someone to trust a 19-year-old with the biggest investment of their life?” Quillo wondered when he started his career.


He soon realized that his experience with digital tools and social media could help him stand out in his local market and build credibility.


Today, Quillo stays top of mind with current and prospective clients by sharing real estate content on Instagram and TikTok.


“Social media is becoming more and more important,” said Quillo. “If as an agent, you’re not using social media, you’re not fully giving everything to your client.”


For Mittelsteadt, establishing credibility meant showing that her knowledge mattered more than her age. She made a point of attending industry events and taking on leadership opportunities.


“You have to demonstrate expertise regardless of your age,” she said.


Like Quillo, Mittelsteadt uses social media to build familiarity and trust before meeting a prospective client in person. She particularly enjoys creating videos that give people a sense of her personality and how she communicates.


“My clients get to know me before they get to meet me,” she said. “It gives them a little bit of familiarity and confidence in who they’re meeting before that first handshake.”


**Finding Support through REMAX**


Both agents credit their REMAX brokerages for helping them establish themselves in the profession.


As a young agent still learning business, Quillo was looking for professional resources and experienced agents he could turn to for guidance.


“When I eventually sat down with the people at REMAX, there was a sense of community,” he said. “Even though REMAX is so big, there is support throughout the brand you can lean on.”


For Mittelsteadt, encouragement from the leadership team at REMAX Excel played an important role in her decision to pursue a career in real estate.


“They believed in me before I believed in myself,” she said.


Since joining REMAX, she has taken advantage of opportunities to attend events and connect with other agents. Those experiences have helped her become more comfortable and confident.


**Advice for Aspiring Agents**


Both Quillo and Mittelsteadt see increased interest in real estate among younger people, but say aspiring agents should make sure they understand what it takes to succeed.


Quillo has noticed more high school seniors taking real estate courses and expressing interest in starting their own businesses.


His advice for those considering the profession is to research and interview with brokerages, find a strong support system and be prepared for a slow start.


“If you’re consistent and stick with it, you’ll be successful,” said Quillo.


Mittelsteadt believes real estate influencers and reality television shows have contributed to that interest. However, she cautions that the reality of working as an agent can be quite different from what people see on screen.


“The appeal of setting your own schedule and being your own boss is real, but so are the responsibilities that come with running a business,” said Mittelsteadt.


She encourages aspiring agents to approach real estate as entrepreneurs rather than simply viewing it as a job.


“Treating it like a true business as an owner and entrepreneur will provide the best framework for longevity,” she said.


Mittelsteadt also encourages young agents to embrace the perspective they bring to the profession while remaining open to learning from others.


“Whether you’re just getting started or years into your career, you will learn every single day,” she said.
